Area.evidence_source: Many men experienced a variety of mental health problems, including substance use problems, without labeling their experiences as a mental health problem. Oftentimes they indicated that they had denied having a problem or felt that they could cope on their own. For example, men with substance use problems did not always seek assistance because they hoped to control their use or were unwilling to acknowledge that substance use was creating problems in their lives. Conversely, some men used alcohol, drugs, or sex to escape from their mental health problems as indicated in the following comments: Men who denied a problem or tried to cope with it themselves tended to be socially isolated, intentionally and/or as a result of past and current behaviors. Denial or inadequate coping techniques were believed to result in the persistence of problems, escalation of symptoms, and suicide attempts.
